title: Business plan readiness
summary: A readiness review for the plan's stated audience, investor or lender. Sets the narrative's assumptions against the financial model and lists each place they disagree, ties out and checks the statements, applies the audience's checklist, and ranks unsupported assumptions. The owner resolves each one at the checkpoint.
notes: Reports consistency and readiness; gives no view on whether to invest or lend.
Lenders set their own debt service coverage thresholds; take the number from the lender.

config.instructions: apply the items for the stated audience; mark the other audience's not_applicable

checklist.label: Lender: repayment source
checklist.question: For a lender: is the source of repayment stated?

checklist.label: Lender: debt service coverage
checklist.question: For a lender: is debt service coverage shown? (The lender sets its own threshold.)

checklist.label: Lender: collateral
checklist.question: For a lender: is collateral described?

checklist.label: Lender: owner's equity
checklist.question: For a lender: is the owner's equity in the business stated?

checklist.label: Investor: bottom-up market sizing
checklist.question: For an investor: is the market sized bottom-up (customers × price), not as a small share of a large market?

checklist.label: Investor: unit economics
checklist.question: For an investor: are unit economics (acquisition cost, margin, lifetime value) given?

checklist.label: Investor: traction evidence
checklist.question: For an investor: is there evidence of traction (customers, revenue, pilots, letters of intent)?

checklist.label: Investor: use of funds tied to milestones
checklist.question: For an investor: is the use of funds tied to milestones?

config.question: Does the model (its period rows and tables) carry the same figure the narrative states for this assumption?
config.instructions: Compare each narrative assumption with the model's figure for the same thing and period: customers, price, revenue, growth, hiring (against the model's headcount and payroll), timing, funding. Mark contradicted when the model's figure differs beyond rounding, and give both figures in the rationale. Mark consistent only when you can name the model row (T id) or table cell that matches. Mark not_in_model when the model has no figure to compare.

config.question: Is the assumption backed by a linked source, a stated estimate, or nothing?
config.instructions: Rank by weight: an assumption that moves the result a lot and has little support is the most severe. In each rationale, say what the assumption does to the result (revenue, runway, funding need) if it is wrong.
Resolve each unsupported assumption: source it, change it, or accept it as a stated risk (note which)
